rationale: Methods: rate = count__domains__DISTANCE_TRAVEL / n_passages per work (every work has 1 passage). Late = year >= 1876. Within each of 8 genres, equal-weight mean of work rates late minus early; then unweighted mean across genres. Estimate +0.025 passage-rate units; 95% CI [0.004, 0.046] from 1000 bootstrap resamples of works stratified by genre x period. Genre-FE OLS with author-clustered SEs gives a similar +0.024 [0.0005, 0.048]. Six of 8 genres rise (adventure and sensation_mystery fall slightly). Sensitivity: every check stays positive but gets smaller: high-confidence dates only +0.015, one work per author +0.016, dropping 1866-1885 +0.018, 1850-1899 window +0.018. By origin: UK +0.033, US +0.019. Decade means rise roughly from ~0.03-0.07 before 1850 to ~0.11-0.12 after 1890. Coverage: only 752 early works, some early genre cells have about 40 works (collection, romance), and early romance's 0 rate inflates the effect. Each work contributes one passage. Alternative explanations: noisy early estimates from small cells; changes in which works and genres were sampled; date misassignment; prolific authors; and annotation drift rather than real change. The cited passages are coded DISTANCE_TRAVEL and only illustrate the construct. They cannot establish a trend. Conclusion: a modest increase that is borderline robust. The CI excludes zero, but the lower bound is near zero and the robustness checks shrink the effect.
